content:
In June this year, we reported on three cases of apps from clients of US-sanctioned Russian banks successfully appearing on the App Store. Two months later, another similar example has made it to the top of the iPhone App Store.

The latest example is K8CHEN PRO. On the App Store, this app is disguised as an augmented reality (AR) kitchen design tool.

Upon opening the app, its flaws are immediately apparent. Its privacy policy link is listed on the App Store, with the content clearly stating it was generated by a "Free Privacy Policy Generator"—this in itself may be a red flag.

Regardless, this app is undoubtedly T-Bank's client application. What interests me is how these apps can repeatedly pass through App Store's review mechanism.

When they receive enough attention and climb up the App Store rankings, it becomes obvious that these apps shouldn't be there at all. The situation is truly baffling.

The two cases reported in June can be seen [here] and [there].

Update: As expected, the app has already been removed from the App Store.

Make the most of your Apple products
